**Status: NOT YET RUN.**

Neither path has been run on the six briefs, so every cell below is empty on purpose. The one-prompt animation run does not exist until the planning and animatic phases of docs/ANIMATION_PIPELINE_RFC.md land. Nothing here is an estimate.

Method: docs/ANIMATION_PIPELINE_RFC.md §8.3. Each brief is a 30–45 second 9:16 Short, run once through `launchclip make --animation` and once through the create-video skill, and scored from the files each run leaves (docs/ANIMATION_MEASUREMENT.md). make is at parity on a brief when every numeric metric is within 15% of the skill's (fewer repair passes, blocking findings or retake rounds than the skill is not a miss), the same gates pass, and the critic's verdict is no worse. Cost and wall-clock time are shown and do not decide parity.

## 1. A problem and a fix (`product-fix`)

> A 35-second vertical animated Short with two characters. A cafe owner keeps losing orders she writes on sticky notes; her friend shows her a shared order board on a tablet; she tries it and the next rush goes smoothly. Play it as a scene between the two of them, not as an advert read by a narrator.

Exercises: two characters who both speak and both act; the problem landing inside the profile's limit; a product shown through what a character does with it, not through narration; the whole chain of contracts on the plainest case.

Not run: neither path has a finished project for this brief.

## 4. An argument (`argument`)

> A 40-second vertical animated Short. Two flatmates argue about whether plates need rinsing before they go in the dishwasher. It is almost all dialogue, each of them sure they are right, and by the end one of them is shown to be wrong.

Exercises: dense dialogue: speaker turns per minute at the top of the band; the speaker on screen on every line, with reactions from the listener; the longest stretch on one framing when two people stand and talk; lip sync under fast back-and-forth.

## 5. A silent story (`silent`)

> A 30-second vertical animated Short with almost no dialogue. One character tries to put together a flat-pack chair without reading the instructions while a second character watches. Tell it through what they do and how they look; at most two lines are spoken.

Exercises: silent lines and their lengths in the script contract; acting carrying the story: poses, expressions and actions per minute; captions, the mix and the lip-sync gate with almost no speech; a character who acts and never speaks still counting as used.

## 6. Three characters, one nearly silent (`trio`)

> A 40-second vertical animated Short with three characters. Two colleagues plan a surprise party in loud whispers across a desk; the third, who the party is for, sits between them wearing headphones and says one line at the very end.

Exercises: three characters kept apart: three voices, three designs, each with its own must_keep; staging three people in 9:16 without anyone leaving the safe area; a character who barely speaks staying present through reactions; every listed character speaking or acting.
